flags.message: The provisioned 63-page OCR application is marked nontruncated but contains the application and an appendix table of contents, not the cited appendix orders and exhibits. It ends with a notice that additional material is available in the Clerk's Office. I treated quoted lower-court findings, the foreclosure notice, and valuation evidence as the applicant's account rather than independently verified appendix evidence. Prediction completed from the available record; this is not asserted to be a provisioning failure.

The provisioned 38-page application is nonempty and marked untruncated, but contains only an index to appendices A–Y and a closing notice that additional material is available in the Clerk's Office. The indexed state orders, accommodation evidence, transcript, and federal orders were not available as primary texts in this record. The forecast attributes their descriptions to the applicant and does not treat them as independently verified. This is an evidentiary limitation, not a missing-snapshot or package-provisioning blocker.

The provisioned appendix is marked truncated, and its pipeline omission begins during the central NMCCA Rule 403 analysis at App. 104, removing the remainder of that opinion, including App. 104-106 cited by the petition. Other record excerpts are also cut. Available App. 98-104 and 201-202 were used; the petition's account of omitted reasoning could not be independently checked. Prediction completed conservatively; no outcome material was sought.

Conservative disclosure: searches to locate the pre-baseline Anderson/Intel circuit opinion incidentally surfaced a commentator's bottom-line expectation concerning related Intel litigation, plus later snippets mentioning government briefing in Parker-Hannifin. The related-case forecast is not a forecast of this cell. I did not open the commentary pages, infer the SG recommendation, or use those bottom lines; substantive external reliance is confined to the May 2025 Anderson and England circuit opinions. No own-case disposition was sought or knowingly incorporated. Context designates forward mode, so later non-outcome material is not itself replay leakage.

Forward cell with a snapshot cut at 2025-07-01, run on 2026-11-13. I carry an unverified recollection from training that the Solicitor General later recommended a grant and that certiorari was granted in No. 24-1030. I did not retrieve the docket or any coverage to check it and reasoned from the pre-cutoff record (probability 0.52), but the recollection may have shaded the number upward; the cell may also be mis-provisioned as forward if the petition is in fact already resolved.

Upstream supremecourt.gov docket JSON (record/snapshots/2026-11-12.json) lists LowerCourt as 'United States Bankruptcy Appellate Panel for the 10th Circuit' for case number (26-2404), whereas record/documents/application.txt and Fourth Circuit No. 26-2404 (In re: Paul Schultz, Oct. 22, 2026) confirm the application arises from the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit (submitted to Chief Justice Roberts as Fourth Circuit Justice).

The staged November 12 snapshot labels the lower tribunal United States Bankruptcy Appellate Panel for the 10th Circuit, No. 26-2404. The staged application instead expressly arises from the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit, identifies Fourth Circuit No. 26-2404, and seeks preservation while that court considers rehearing. Review/correct the upstream lower-court metadata. This discrepancy does not prevent scoring the recorded November 11 denial.

The snapshot's LowerCourt field reads 'United States Bankruptcy Appellate Panel for the 10th Circuit' with case number 26-2404, but the staged application's own cover says it arises from the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit (No. 26-2404), and it was submitted to the Chief Justice. The lower-court label looks wrong upstream. It did not change any score.

All three candidates report that the application text they were given was empty (documents.json empty_text true, fetched Nov 6), while the copy staged for the evaluator (fetched 2026-11-11) carries OCR text. The predictors therefore forecast without the application's content. I did not penalize them for it.

This affects reasoning_quality, not the mechanical probability score or harness-stamped baseline.

The evaluator's documents.json instead describes a November 11 OCR extraction with empty_text=false. The later text is available now; the historical gap is disclosed so candidates are not penalized for failing to read content supplied only later.

Reflected in reasoning_quality only; no score depends on it.

All three candidates report record/documents/application.txt as empty_text (61 scanned pages, no text layer) at prediction time; the evaluator's record carries an OCR'd text. Predictors forecast without the application's content.

While running google_web_search restricted with site:supremecourt.gov to check whether companion ERISA split cases (Trauernicht, Cedeno, Parker, Platt) had Supreme Court dockets, Gemini's search grounding metadata included a citation link to scotusgate.com alongside supremecourt.gov links. Only factual docket dates and question-presented summaries appeared in the search tool text (zero forecast probabilities, predictions, or commentary surfaced), the external link was never opened, and it had no influence on this prediction.

During Google web searches checking whether companion/split decisions (Trauernicht, Parrott, Williams, Platt, Cedeno, Parker) had separate cert petitions, scotusgate.com appeared among grounding source URLs (never opened or fetched) and Gemini Search's AI-synthesized overview generically described No. 26-267 as 'the most active and likely candidate for a grant of certiorari' / 'expected to address' the split, with no numerical odds or forecast details. This generic search synthesis was immediately set aside and disregarded, and it did not shape the prediction (P(grant) = 0.24, predicting denial).

Petition page 14 says Judge VanDyke did not opine on the scope of appropriate relief. The provisioned appendix at 25a instead expressly agrees with the majority's propositions permitting plan-wide financial and equitable recovery, before dissenting on contract interpretation and delegation. I relied on the opinion itself and did not count the panel dissent as supporting petitioners on the question presented. This is a characterization discrepancy in party advocacy, not a provisioning failure.

(Corrected)' (after an initial 'not accepted for filing' entry the same day), which predates the 2026-11-05 cutoff and postdates the Jun 29 2026 cert grant, but merits-amicus-united-states.txt is absent from record/documents/documents.json—likely because the 'supporting vacatur' or '(Corrected)' phrasing or the preceding rejection entry missed the document-staging matcher. Both parties' merits briefs and sg-invited-brief.txt were staged, and Respondent's merits brief cites and summarizes SG.Br. directly.

The snapshot records the September 15, 2026 corrected United States merits amicus brief supporting vacatur, but documents.json and the provisioned documents omit merits-amicus-united-states.txt. The staged sg-invited-brief.txt is the different May 20 cert-stage filing. Recovered and used the corrected merits PDF through the official Supreme Court docket; it predates the November 5 cutoff. The gap did not block the forecast.

The snapshot shows 'Brief amicus curiae of United States supporting vacatur filed. (Corrected)' on Sep 15 2026, after the grant and before the cutoff, but record/documents/ holds no merits-amicus-united-states.txt and documents.json has no row for it. Forecast used only the docket caption and the respondent's citations to that brief.

In record/documents/petition.txt (106 pages, empty_text=false, ocr_derived=false), the front matter (cover, Questions Presented, Table of Contents, Table of Authorities, pp. i-xi) and the entire Appendix (pp. 1a-63a) extracted cleanly, but pages 1-29 of the Petition body extracted as ~45 blank lines (lines 286-331) with no pipeline truncation note, suggesting mixed PDF text/image layers where overall text volume masked empty body pages from OCR fallback.

record/documents/lower-court-docket.txt reports 'petition filed: none' and 'disposition: not found' for rehearing en banc because the 4 post-judgment RECAP docket entries on CourtListener (docket 68399001, entries 64, 65, 73, 76 between 2026-07-15 and 2026-08-11) have blank description strings; Petition Appendix A (petition.txt, pp. 1a-2a) shows that Petitioners did petition for rehearing en banc and the Fourth Circuit denied it on 2026-08-11 with no judge requesting a poll.

petition.txt has front matter and an extensive appendix but no readable numbered petition body pp. 1–29: it moves from appendix contents to appendix A. documents.json nevertheless marks it nonempty and untruncated. The official PDF open failed. Forecast uses the QP, contents headings, decision below and appendix, not the absent substantive argument. Consider checking page-level extraction or adding OCR for the missing body.

lower-court-docket.txt reports no rehearing petition found and no disposition found in its four-entry read, but petition appendix A contains the August 11, 2026 order denying rehearing and rehearing en banc, with no judge requesting a poll. Forecast follows the appendix rather than interpreting the summary as absence of rehearing.

record/documents/petition.txt carries the questions presented, tables of contents and authorities, and the appendix, but not the petition's body (introduction, statement, reasons for granting, pp. 1-29). documents.json reports truncated: false and the text has no pipeline note marking a cut. The forecast read the argument from the headings and the appendix only.
